correctness.rationale: Away from null directions, project the central cut down to the base. It is the base intersected with the strip between the projected cap lines, with thresholds ±q for q=λ|U_z|/√(1−U_z²). If the cap lines cut the base, there are four new cap/base-edge intersections, and every original vertex within the strip contributes one section vertex. Symmetry pairs the surviving base vertices. The most possible is 2m−2 survivors plus four, and this occurs exactly between the second-largest and largest projected magnitudes from the m antipodal pairs. When the caps are not cut, the section has 2m sides. On the uniform folded azimuth [0,θ], the two largest magnitudes are a=cos φ and b=cos(2θ−φ). Integrating the independent uniform |U_z| gives a/√(λ²+a²)−b/√(λ²+b²); the azimuth antiderivative is arcsin(t sin φ), with the argument adjusted for the second term. Differentiating in t, the difference of the squared positive bracket terms has the sign of 1−3cos²θ t². The unique optimizer lies in (0,1), gives λ²=3cos²θ−1 under the half-height convention, and substitution yields the optimum. Taylor expansion gives bracket θ³t(1−t²)+O(θ⁵), so at t→1/√3 the coefficient of m⁻² is π²/(6√3). The hexagon value agrees under the same normalization.
residual_risks: Only nonexceptional directions need be classified for probability. The quadrature is diagnostic; it does not certify the continuum optimizer or asymptotics.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The generic polygon formula specializes to these strips but is later; the unequal-sided cuboid case does not include bases of ≥6 sides. Cube volume criticality and chamber combinatorics alone are not the optimization theorem. The earlier b6d28d7c72f4 already covers the full regular range regardless.

originality.rationale: The earlier indexed Resultary record b6d28d7c72f4 states the same theorem for every even n≥6 under circumradius one and caps at ±h. With n=2m and scale h→h/R it gives the identical all-height maximal-side Haar law, the identical unique optimizer and hexagonal example, and the identical optimized large-base limit. The explicit p_m* formula substitutes the previously known optimizer into the already-stated exact law. No substantive remainder of the frozen finding survives this comparison; this is direct prior coverage within the corpus, not a claim about earliest historical publication.
